label: Autoplay Control
title: Autoplay Control
summary: Let people pause and resume content that advances on its own, such as a slideshow.
corePrinciple: Show the action a press will take: pause while content plays, play while it is stopped.

anatomy.title: A fixed circle around one icon
anatomy.description: The control is a single pressable circle. Its state property decides whether the icon is pause or play.
blocks: A 36 × 36 circle. Width, height, radius, and the white fill come from Autoplay Control tokens.
Shown for state="pause", the default, while content advances.
Shown for state="play", while content is stopped. Both icons are 24 px and black.

configuration.title: One property: the action to offer
configuration.description: state swaps the icon between pause and play. Nothing else changes: tokens fix the circle and its colors in a single mode, and the icon is always 24 px.
blocks: The default. It tells people a press will stop the slideshow, video, or audio.
Shown after playback stops. A press should start it again.

states.title: Enabled, pressed, and unavailable
states.description: disabled fades the control and ignores presses. Pressed feedback is shown only while a pointer is down.
blocks: Half opacity. Presses are ignored and the control leaves the Tab order.
While pressed, the control drops to 70% opacity. It adds no hover style of its own; keyboard focus shows the browser’s standard focus ring. Try it in the live example above.

sizing.title: Tokens fix the size
sizing.description: The control does not stretch or shrink with its host. Leave room around the 36 px circle so it is easy to press.

content.title: The icon is the whole message
content.description: The control shows no text. Its icon has to describe what a press will do, and nearby content has to show what is playing.
blocks: Show the action, not the status
While slides advance, show pause. When they stop, show play.
Carousel’s Numbered type places the control beside NumberPagination, so people can see which slide is showing.
Canonical guidance names video, audio, and slideshow playback as its uses.

inContext.title: Pause and resume a slideshow

doDont.title: Keep the icon honest and visible
doDont.description: The control only works when its icon matches what the content is doing and its white circle stands out from the surface.
blocks: The icon matches what a press will do: stop the slides.
The play icon suggests the slides are already stopped, so people cannot tell how to pause them.
Place it on media or a dark surface
The white circle stands out, so the target is easy to find.
Place it on a white surface
The white circle disappears, leaving an unbounded glyph with no visible target.

sources.title: Public AutoplayControl and its Carousel composition
sources.description: The guide renders the public jfs-components AutoplayControl on its own and inside the public Carousel.

AutoplayControl docs and stories; Carousel Numbered story

Declared and installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s state variants match the package’s state property. The control is named “Pause” or “Play” after its state; developers can set a more specific accessibilityLabel, such as “Pause slideshow”, as Storybook asks. The control has no timer: Carousel’s Numbered type owns autoplay, with a 4-second default interval.
